full_text_en:
Liu Qishan, Fan Zhanwu, and Liu Ning — Smuggling, Offering Bribes, and Accepting Bribes

Defendant Liu Qishan, male, 48 years old, former Director of Rushan City Commercial Bureau, Shandong Province, arrested on August 7, 1993.

Defendant Fan Zhanwu, male, 40 years old, former Political Commissar of the Border Defense Sub-bureau of Weihai City Public Security Bureau, Shandong Province, arrested on October 9, 1993.

Defendant Liu Ning, male, 38 years old, former Deputy Director of the Operations Division of the Border Defense Sub-bureau of Weihai City Public Security Bureau, Shandong Province, arrested on October 10, 1993.

The Weihai City People's Procuratorate, Shandong Province, initiated a public prosecution with the Weihai Intermediate People's Court against Defendant Liu Qishan for committing the crimes of smuggling, offering bribes, and accepting bribes; and against Defendants Fan Zhanwu and Liu Ning for committing the crimes of smuggling and accepting bribes.

The Weihai Intermediate People's Court, after trial, found the following facts:

In October 1992, having learned that a subordinate unit of the Commercial Bureau had been caught smuggling, Defendant Liu Qishan, during his tenure as Director of Rushan City Commercial Bureau, Shandong Province, became acquainted with Defendants Fan Zhanwu and Liu Ning, as well as co-defendant Yan Shili (former Head of the Operations Division of the Border Defense Sub-bureau of Weihai City Public Security Bureau, already sentenced). Thereafter, in order to facilitate smuggling activities by the Rushan City commercial system, Liu Qishan repeatedly offered bribes and hosted banquets for Fan Zhanwu, Liu Ning, and Yan Shili. Fan Zhanwu, Liu Ning, and Yan Shili promised to provide favorable treatment for the smuggling activities of the Rushan City commercial system.

In early to mid-July 1993, in order to enable his unit to obtain illegal profits from the smuggling activities of other units in the form of fines, and to legitimize smuggling activities, Fan Zhanwu, together with Liu Ning, formulated an "Urgent Notice on Issues Concerning Smuggling Units Voluntarily Surrendering Themselves in Accordance with Regulations." The Notice stipulated that smuggling units must "voluntarily surrender" to the Border Defense Sub-bureau of Weihai City Public Security Bureau, and after such surrender, the smuggled goods could be disposed of by fines on a cost-recovery principle. Before the Notice was issued, Fan Zhanwu and Liu Ning, based on prior promises, telephoned Liu Qishan to inform him of their intent and the content of the Notice, hinting that Liu Qishan could take advantage of this opportunity to engage in smuggling. Liu Qishan then discussed with Li Naiming (Deputy Director of the Commercial Bureau, currently at large) and others, and decided that the Commercial Bureau should take this opportunity to smuggle cigarettes. Liu Qishan and Li Naiming actively contacted smugglers from Fujian Province and Hong Kong, repeatedly assuring them that the smuggling activities would be protected by border defense personnel and would be safe. On July 16, co-defendants Qiu Guojian (from Shishi City, Fujian Province, already sentenced) and Fu Mingsheng (from Shishi City, Fujian Province, currently at large), dispatched by Hong Kong smugglers, arrived in Rushan City. After contacting the smuggling vessel using an illegally installed radio at a subordinate unit of the Rushan City Commercial Bureau, they told Li Naiming that the cigarette-laden smuggling vessel was at sea and requested personnel to go out to sea to meet the vessel. Upon learning this, Liu Qishan telephoned Fan Zhanwu and proposed smuggling a batch of cigarettes. Fan Zhanwu told Liu Qishan that a direct forced landing would not work and that he should bring a remittance certificate in foreign currency and go through the "voluntary surrender" procedures at the Weihai Border Defense Sub-bureau as previously arranged. Liu Qishan agreed to send someone to "surrender," and at the same time requested Fan Zhanwu to send personnel to sea to "escort back" the smuggled goods and to negotiate with the customs authorities. Fan Zhanwu agreed and arranged for Yan Shili to negotiate with customs. On the morning of July 17, Liu Qishan and Li Naiming, as requested by Fan Zhanwu and Liu Ning, sent co-defendant Jiang Hai (former cadre of Rushan City Commercial Bureau, already sentenced) to Liu Ning with a photocopy of a forged remittance certificate stub to complete the "voluntary surrender" procedures. Subsequently, Liu Ning suggested that Fan Zhanwu immediately dispatch troops to sea to escort the vessel. Fan Zhanwu then assigned co-defendant Wang Weidong (former Deputy Chief of Staff of the Border Defense Sub-bureau of Weihai City Public Security Bureau, already sentenced) to lead Staff Officer Zhang and two soldiers, armed with four submachine guns, to Rushan to go out to sea and meet the smuggling vessel. Liu Qishan, under the pretext of "hardship allowance," instructed Li Naiming to give Wang Weidong RMB 5,000 and requested him to underreport the quantity of smuggled cigarettes. On the afternoon of July 18, Wang Weidong and the other four armed personnel, along with Jiang Hai and Fu Mingsheng, boarded the smuggling vessel at sea after rendezvousing with it on the fishing vessel "Lu Ru Bu 1039," which had been chartered by co-defendant Wang Xuefeng (former Political Instructor of Rushan Border Defense Brigade, already sentenced) at Liu Qishan's request. Upon learning that the vessel was carrying more than 9,900 cartons of smuggled cigarettes, Wang Weidong, after consulting with Staff Officer Zhang, planned to falsely report the quantity as 3,000 to 4,000 cartons, and gave Zhang RMB 2,000 from the RMB 5,000 received. On the morning of July 19, Liu Qishan learned that the smuggling vessel would arrive at port in the afternoon, and he organized personnel to prepare for unloading and selling at the port. He also requested Liu Tongxiao (Director of Rushan City Public Security Bureau, currently at large) and co-defendant Sun Xiping (former Deputy Director of Rushan City Public Security Bureau, already sentenced) to send police officers to the dock to "maintain order." At about 3:00 p.m. that day, the smuggling vessel docked at Rushankou Port. Sun Xiping and Wang Xuefeng led more than 20 police officers, dispatched three police cars to the dock to "maintain order." At that time, Weihai Customs officers arrived at the scene to perform anti-smuggling duties. Wang Weidong immediately reported to Fan Zhanwu. Fan Zhanwu, claiming that the case was a "voluntary surrender" case accepted by the Border Defense Sub-bureau, intervened with the Weihai Customs, resulting in the withdrawal of the Weihai Customs officers. Wang Weidong informed Liu Qishan of the actual quantity of cigarettes on the smuggling vessel, and they agreed to falsely report the quantity as 3,000 cartons. At about 6:00 p.m. that day, a Qingdao Customs anti-smuggling boat arrived at Rushankou Port to stop the unloading of cigarettes. Fan Zhanwu again intervened to prevent the customs officers from performing their anti-smuggling duties, and the two sides were at a standoff for more than 40 hours. During this period, the customs officers, after repeated negotiations with Fan Zhanwu, agreed that no cigarettes would be unloaded, the smuggling vessel would not leave the dock, and both sides would send personnel to monitor. The customs officers, unable to perform their anti-smuggling duties and to prevent a larger conflict, withdrew at noon on July 21. After the customs officers left, Wang Xuefeng, who was responsible for monitoring the smuggling vessel, immediately telephoned Liu Qishan. Liu Qishan immediately organized personnel, with the consent of Yan Shili and the protection of Sun Xiping and others, to unload and sell all the smuggled cigarettes. Subsequently, to conceal the actual quantity of smuggled cigarettes, Liu Qishan instructed Yan Shili to seal up 3,000 cartons of smuggled cigarettes. The total quantity of cigarettes smuggled on this occasion was 9,953 cartons, with a value of RMB 22,082,820.

After the incident, to deal with investigations by relevant authorities, Defendant Fan Zhanwu instructed Yan Shili, Wang Xuefeng, and others to fabricate a certification document stating that Liu Qishan of the Rushan City Commercial Bureau had smuggled 3,000 cartons of cigarettes and that the decision to unload was made by them, in order to conceal and mitigate the facts and responsibility of the Rushan City Commercial Bureau's smuggling of cigarettes. On July 26, after Defendant Liu Qishan was detained, Fan Zhanwu, at the instruction of Wang Jianzhi (former Secretary of the Rushan City Municipal Party Committee and co-defendant, already sentenced), went to the detention center and told Liu Qishan, and also notified other persons with knowledge and responsibility, to coordinate their statements and conceal the true facts, helping Liu Qishan and others evade legal sanctions.

In addition to the above facts, Defendant Liu Qishan, from December 1992 to June 1993, participated on three occasions in the smuggling of 13,800 cartons of cigarettes by the People's Market, a brewing factory, and other subordinate units of the Rushan City Commercial Bureau, with a total value of more than RMB 27 million. From March to July 1993, to facilitate smuggling activities by the commercial system, Liu Qishan, on five occasions, used public funds to offer bribes in cash and goods totaling RMB 41,230.55 to Fan Zhanwu, Liu Ning, Yan Shili, and others. From March to July 1993, Liu Qishan also accepted bribes on eight occasions from subordinate units and individuals of the Rushan City Commercial Bureau, including RMB 3,200 in cash and items such as a television, air conditioner, camera, and component stereo system, with the total value of cash and goods received amounting to RMB 621,127.50.

Defendant Fan Zhanwu, from November 1992 to June 1993, took advantage of his position to accept bribes on eleven occasions from smuggling units and individuals, including RMB 114,600 in cash, USD 1,000, and items such as a television, air conditioner, video camera, and gold jewelry, with the total value of cash and goods received amounting to RMB 154,064.35.

Defendant Liu Ning, together with Yan Shili, directly purchased and sold three smuggled cars from Rongcheng City Xixiakou Fishery Company in April 1993, with the smuggled cars valued at RMB 13,500 (should be 135,000? Furthermore, from March to June 1993, Liu Ning took advantage of his position to accept bribes on twelve occasions from smuggling units and individuals including the Rushan City Commercial Bureau, totaling RMB 233,500 in cash and items such as motorcycles, air conditioners, televisions, and gold jewelry, with the total value of cash and goods received amounting to RMB 258,087.6.

The above facts are confirmed by physical evidence such as seized illicit money and goods, documentary evidence, witness testimony, and the confessions of co-defendants, as well as the confessions of Defendants Liu Qishan, Fan Zhanwu, and Liu Ning.

The Weihai Intermediate People's Court held that: The co-defendant Rushan County Commercial Bureau, in violation of customs regulations and evading customs supervision, smuggled cigarettes valued at RMB 22,082,820. Its conduct violated Article 5, paragraph 2 of the "Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Punishing the Crime of Smuggling," constituting the crime of smuggling, and should be sentenced to a fine in accordance with this paragraph.

Defendant Liu Qishan, as the directly responsible supervisor of the smuggling crime of the Rushan City Commercial Bureau, has committed the crime of smuggling. Furthermore, in the smuggling activities, he colluded with Fan Zhanwu, Liu Ning, and others, and requested Fan Zhanwu and Liu Ning to send troops out to sea to meet the smuggling vessel and provide armed escort for the smuggling activities, making him a principal offender in this case. Liu Qishan's smuggling amount was particularly huge, and the circumstances were particularly severe. In accordance with Article 10, paragraph 1 and Article 1 of the Supplementary Provisions on Punishing the Crime of Smuggling, he should be severely punished. Liu Qishan, for the smuggling activities of the Rushan City Commercial Bureau and its subordinate units, offered bribes to Fan Zhanwu, Liu Ning, and others on five occasions, and as the directly responsible supervisor of the bribery by the Rushan City Commercial Bureau, his conduct violated Article 9 of the "Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Punishing the Crimes of Embezzlement and Bribery," constituting the crime of offering bribes. Liu Qishan, taking advantage of his position, accepted bribes, and his conduct violated Article 4 of the Supplementary Provisions on Punishing the Crimes of Embezzlement and Bribery, constituting the crime of accepting bribes. The amount of bribes he accepted was particularly huge, and the circumstances were particularly severe. He should be severely punished in accordance with Article 5 of the Supplementary Provisions on Punishing the Crimes of Embezzlement and Bribery. Defendant Fan Zhanwu actively participated in the smuggling of cigarettes by the Rushan City Commercial Bureau, assigned armed personnel to meet the smuggling vessel at sea, and provided armed escort for the smuggling. His conduct constituted the crime of smuggling, and he committed the smuggling crime by taking advantage of his position to suppress smuggling. He played a major role in the smuggling crime as a principal offender, with particularly severe circumstances, and should be severely punished according to law. Fan Zhanwu, taking advantage of his position, accepted bribes from smuggling units and individuals, and his conduct constituted the crime of accepting bribes. The amount was particularly huge, the circumstances were particularly severe, and he should be severely punished according to law. Defendant Liu Ning, taking advantage of his position, actively participated in the smuggling of cigarettes by the Rushan City Commercial Bureau, urged Fan Zhanwu to send troops to sea to meet the smuggling vessel, and provided armed escort for the smuggling. His conduct constituted the crime of smuggling, and he committed the smuggling crime by taking advantage of his position to suppress smuggling, with particularly severe circumstances, and should be given a heavier punishment according to law. Liu Ning, taking advantage of his position, accepted and demanded bribes from smuggling units and individuals, and his conduct constituted the crime of accepting bribes. The amount was particularly huge, the circumstances were particularly severe, and he should be severely punished according to law. All three defendants committed multiple crimes, and should be subject to concurrent punishment for multiple crimes in accordance with Article 64 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China. The three defendants should also have their political rights deprived for life in accordance with Article 53, paragraph 1 of the Criminal Law. Accordingly, the Weihai Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on February 8, 1994: Defendant Liu Qishan was sentenced to death for the crime of smuggling, with deprivation of political rights for life; sentenced to life imprisonment for the crime of accepting bribes, with deprivation of political rights for life; sentenced to three years' imprisonment for the crime of offering bribes; and the combined sentence was execution by death, with deprivation of political rights for life. Defendant Fan Zhanwu was sentenced to death for the crime of smuggling, with deprivation of political rights for life; sentenced to death for the crime of accepting bribes, with deprivation of political rights for life; and the combined sentence was execution by death, with deprivation of political rights for life. Defendant Liu Ning was sentenced to life imprisonment for the crime of smuggling, with deprivation of political rights for life; sentenced to death for the crime of accepting bribes, with deprivation of political rights for life; and the combined sentence was execution by death, with deprivation of political rights for life.

After the first instance judgment was pronounced, Defendants Liu Qishan, Fan Zhanwu, and Liu Ning appealed to the Shandong High People's Court. Liu Qishan's grounds for appeal were: that the smuggling was intended to generate income for the collective, that he was induced and instigated by Fan Zhanwu and Liu Ning, that he did not request armed escort from the Weihai Border Defense Sub-bureau, that he had performed meritorious service by reporting others' smuggling crimes, and that he had a good attitude in admitting his guilt, so he should receive a lighter punishment. Fan Zhanwu's grounds for appeal were: that the Weihai Public Security Bureau Border Defense Sub-bureau, acting on the instructions of superiors, formulated the "Urgent Notice on Issues Concerning Smuggling Units Voluntarily Surrendering Themselves in Accordance with Regulations," which provided for fines on a cost-recovery principle; that the appellant was merely escorting the voluntarily surrendering smuggling vessel in accordance with this Notice, not providing armed escort for smuggling, and therefore did not commit the crime of smuggling. Liu Ning's grounds for appeal were: that he did not participate in formulating the "Urgent Notice on Issues Concerning Smuggling Units Voluntarily Surrendering Themselves in Accordance with Regulations," nor did he urge Fan Zhanwu to send troops to escort the smuggling; that he was not a directly responsible person in this case; and that he had performed meritorious service by reporting others' smuggling crimes, so he should receive a lighter punishment.

The Shandong High People's Court, after trial, held that: Appellant Liu Qishan's argument that the smuggling was intended to generate income for the collective cannot mitigate his criminal liability for the crime of smuggling, as his conduct was not lawful. The claims by Liu Qishan that he did not request armed escort and that he had performed meritorious service by reporting others' smuggling crimes; by Appellant Fan Zhanwu that he formulated and implemented the document on the instructions of superiors; and by Appellant Liu Ning that he did not participate in formulating the document, did not urge the dispatch of troops for smuggling escort, and had performed meritorious service by reporting others' smuggling crimes, were all found to be untrue upon investigation. Therefore, the grounds of appeal of the three appellants were untenable. The facts of the crime found in the first instance judgment were clear, the evidence was reliable and sufficient, the conviction was accurate, the sentence was appropriate, and the trial procedure was lawful. Accordingly, the Shandong High People's Court, in accordance with Article 136, item (1) of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered a ruling on May 11, 1994: Appeal dismissed, original judgment affirmed.

Pursuant to Article 144 of the Criminal Procedure Law, the Shandong High People's Court submitted the ruling affirming the first instance death sentences, with deprivation of political rights for life, imposed on Liu Qishan, Fan Zhanwu, and Liu Ning to the Supreme People's Court for approval.

The Supreme People's Court, after review, rendered a ruling on May 23, 1994:

Approved the criminal ruling of the Shandong High People's Court affirming the first instance judgment imposing upon Defendant Liu Qishan the death penalty for the crime of smuggling, with deprivation of political rights for life; life imprisonment for the crime of accepting bribes, with deprivation of political rights for life; three years' imprisonment for the crime of offering bribes; and the combined sentence of execution by death, with deprivation of political rights for life; imposing upon Defendant Fan Zhanwu the death penalty for the crime of smuggling, with deprivation of political rights for life; the death penalty for the crime of accepting bribes, with deprivation of political rights for life; and the combined sentence of execution by death, with deprivation of political rights for life; imposing upon Defendant Liu Ning life imprisonment for the crime of smuggling, with deprivation of political rights for life; the death penalty for the crime of accepting bribes, with deprivation of political rights for life; and the combined sentence of execution by death, with deprivation of political rights for life.
